explicit_validation.explanation: Paper explicitly validates OpenCHAIR's LLM-based evaluation against human judgments on the same set of instances, reporting balanced accuracy metrics comparing object-level decisions

prompts.notes: Exact prompt template shown in main text: "<s>[INST] An image has the following caption: "⟨input caption⟩". Does the image contain the following object? "⟨input object⟩". Answer yes/no/unsure. The answer is: [/INST]"

guidelines.notes: Human annotators classify each predicted object as hallucinated or not based on the image and caption described in appendix section C.2

sample_size.notes: Manual checking of object-level decisions for over 400 random objects across various captioning models

correlation_interpretation.threshold_used: Accuracy comparison only (no specific thresholds mentioned)

validation_results.summary_finding: OpenCHAIR LLM evaluation achieves higher balanced accuracy (0.930-0.945) than CHAIR (0.774-0.899) in predicting human judgments of object hallucinations, despite operating in a more challenging open-vocabulary setting.

criteria_mapping.notes: Both LLM and human evaluation use identical criteria - determining whether predicted objects are present in ground truth or hallucinated
